records.question: How much will my Apex plan pay per day towards the hospital room?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield Version 2 pays **Rs. 7,500 per day** toward the hospital room rent. This is the daily room‑rent sub‑limit specified in the policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: Is there a daily cap on intensive care charges in the Apex plan?
records.answer: No. Under the Apex Health Shield Version 2 policy, ICU/ICCU charges are covered at actual cost with no sub‑limit or daily cap – they are payable up to the sum insured [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: For how many days before admission does the Apex plan cover my medical expenses?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield policy covers medical expenses incurred up to **60 days before admission** (pre‑hospitalisation cover) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: What is the most the Apex plan pays for an ambulance each time I am hospitalised?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield plan covers up to **Rs. 3,500 per hospitalisation** for road ambulance charges. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How much does the Apex plan pay for Ayurveda and other AYUSH treatment?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield plan covers Ayurveda and other AYUSH treatments up to **100 % of the Sum Insured** (subject to the linked‑to‑illness condition)[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: Does the Apex plan put a limit on day care procedures?
records.answer: Yes.  Under Apex Health Shield Version 2, day‑care procedures are covered up to the Sum Insured, but only for an initial period of 30 days [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How long must I wait before the Apex plan pays for an illness that is not an accident?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield policy requires an initial waiting period of **30 days** before it will pay for any illness that is not an accidental bodily injury. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How many months do I have to wait for cataract surgery to be covered on the Apex plan?
records.answer: The waiting period for cataract surgery under the Apex Health Shield Policy (Version 2) is **12 months**. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: When can I claim for hernia or piles treatment on the Apex plan?
records.answer: Claims for hernia or piles treatment can be made only after the 24‑month waiting period has expired. This waiting period applies to all illnesses listed under that category, including hernia, hydrocele, piles and fistula, and no claim will be admissible until the period has lapsed [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: After how long does the Apex plan cover a joint replacement?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield policy requires a waiting period of **24 months** before a joint replacement surgery (unless it is accidental) becomes covered. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How long is the wait for conditions I already had when I bought the Apex plan?
records.answer: The waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at the time of inception of the Apex Health Shield Policy is **36 months**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the most the Apex plan pays per eye for cataract surgery?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield Policy (Version 2) pays up to **Rs. 60,000 per eye** for cataract surgery. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How often can I get a free annual health check-up on the Silver wellness plan?
records.answer: You can receive a free annual health check‑up once per year on the Harbor Wellness Silver plan. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: What is the biggest renewal discount I can earn through steps on the Gold wellness plan?
records.answer: The biggest renewal discount you can earn on the Gold wellness plan is **up to 20%** based on steps. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: How much worldwide emergency cover does the Gold wellness plan give?
records.answer: The Gold wellness plan includes worldwide emergency cover up to $50,000 [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: What is the daily limit on ICU charges under the Harbor wellness plan?
records.answer: There is no daily limit on ICU charges under the Harbor Wellness plan. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: How much air ambulance cover does the Gold wellness plan include?
records.answer: The Gold wellness plan includes air ambulance coverage of up to Rs. 5 Lakhs. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: How much does the critical illness rider pay out if I am diagnosed with cancer?
records.answer: The Critical Illness Rider pays out 100 % of the Rider Sum Insured if you are diagnosed with cancer of specified severity. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: How many days must I survive after a heart attack to claim under the critical illness rider?
records.answer: You must survive **30 days** after a heart attack to claim under the critical illness rider. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What does the critical illness rider pay for kidney failure needing dialysis?
records.answer: The critical illness rider pays **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for kidney failure requiring dialysis. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What commission does an agent in the Silver tier earn?
records.answer: The commission for an agent in the Silver tier is **7%** [AGENT_GUIDE_FAKE p.1].

records.question: How far back does the Apex plan look when deciding if a condition was pre-existing?
records.answer: The Apex plan considers a condition pre‑existing if it was present, diagnosed, or treated within **36 months prior to policy inception**. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1]

records.question: How many days do I have to cancel the Apex plan and get my premium back after buying it?
records.answer: You have a 15‑day free‑look period from the date you receive the policy schedule. Within those 15 days you can cancel the Apex plan and receive a refund of your premium (subject to minimal administrative charges) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: Will the Apex plan pay for cosmetic surgery?
records.answer: No. Cosmetic surgery for aesthetic reasons is excluded from coverage unless it is reconstructive surgery following an accidental bodily injury. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Does the Apex plan pay if someone deliberately injures themselves?
records.answer: No. The Apex Health Shield policy excludes claims that arise from intentional self‑inflicted injury, suicide attempts, or hazardous adventure sports, and such claims are strictly non‑payable. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: How much does the Apex plan pay for maternity?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield plan covers inpatient medical expenses for maternity (normal or cesarean delivery) up to **Rs. 50,000 per delivery** (maximum of two deliveries) after a waiting period of 24 months. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Is surgery for weight loss covered by the Apex plan?
records.answer: No.  Weight‑loss surgery (bariatric surgery) is excluded from coverage under the Apex Health Shield Policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: How early must I tell the insurer before a planned hospital stay on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must notify the insurer at least **48 hours before** a planned admission at a network hospital. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: How soon must I report an emergency admission on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must provide notice of an emergency admission within 24 hours of the emergency hospitalisation or before discharge, whichever comes first. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: How long after I leave hospital do I have to send in my claim papers on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must submit all required claim documents within **30 days of discharge** from the hospital. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: Do older customers pay part of the bill themselves on the Apex plan?
records.answer: Yes. Under Version 2 of the Apex Health Shield Policy, insured persons aged 65 years and above are required to pay a mandatory co‑payment of 10 % of each admissible claim. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: How much does my cover grow each year I make no claim on the Apex plan?
records.answer:
Your cover increases by **20 % of the base Sum Insured for each claim‑free policy year**.  
This growth continues until the cumulative bonus reaches **100 % of the base Sum Insured** (i.e., the cover can double the original base amount at most).  

[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: What is the ceiling on the no-claim growth in cover on the Apex plan?
records.answer: The maximum increase in cover for each claim‑free year (the no‑claim growth) is capped at **100 % of the base Sum Insured**. This ceiling is specified in the policy’s cumulative bonus clause. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: Does the Harbor wellness plan make senior citizens pay a share of the bill?
records.answer: I do not have enough information in the provided policy documents to answer this question.

records.question: How do I cancel the Harbor wellness plan after buying it, within the free-look window?
records.answer:
To cancel your Harbor Wellness plan within the free‑look period, simply send a written notice of cancellation. The free‑look window is 15 days from the date the policy is delivered to you, so you must submit the written notice within that time frame.  

[HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.4]

records.question: How long is the initial waiting period on the critical illness rider?
records.answer: The initial waiting period on the Critical Illness Rider is 90 days from the policy inception [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.2].

records.question: On the Apex plan, how long must I stay in hospital for it to count as inpatient treatment, and what is the daily room limit?
records.answer:
The policy defines an **inpatient hospitalisation** as an admission that lasts for a **minimum of 24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

Under Version 2, the **daily room‑rent allowance** is capped at **Rs. 7,500 per day** for eligible rooms [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How does the Apex plan's definition of a pre-existing condition line up with the waiting period for such conditions?
records.answer:
The Apex Health Shield policy defines a **pre‑existing disease (PED)** as any condition, ailment or injury for which the insured had signs or symptoms, was diagnosed, or received medical advice or treatment within **36 months prior to policy inception** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

The waiting period that applies to such pre‑existing diseases declared at the time of policy inception is also **36 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Thus, the definition of a pre‑existing condition and the waiting period for those conditions are aligned: both are based on a 36‑month period before the policy starts.

records.question: What waiting period and money limit does the Apex plan set for cataract surgery?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield Policy (Version 2) specifies a 12‑month waiting period for cataract surgery, with a sub‑limit of Rs. 60,000 per eye. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How does the maternity waiting period on the Apex plan compare with its general initial waiting period?
records.answer:
The Apex Health Shield policy’s general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  
In contrast, the maternity benefit has a waiting period of **24 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  

Thus, the maternity waiting period is far longer—24 months versus 30 days.

records.question: What does the critical illness rider pay for a major organ transplant, and what extra donor cost does its endorsement add?
records.answer:
The critical illness rider pays **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for a major organ (or bone‑marrow) transplant [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].  

Its endorsement adds coverage for organ‑donor expenses, paying **up to Rs. 2,00,000** for hospitalisation costs incurred during organ donation harvesting from a living donor [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: Did the daily room rent limit on the Apex plan go up or down between the older and newer version?
records.answer: The daily room‑rent limit increased from the older version to the newer version – it rose from Rs. 5,000 per day in Version 1 to Rs. 7,500 per day in Version 2. [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How did the number of days of pre-hospital cover change between the old and new Apex plan?
records.answer:
The pre‑hospitalisation cover was extended from **30 days prior to admission** in the old Apex Health Shield Version 1 to **60 days prior to admission** in the new Version 2, an increase of 30 days.  

- Old plan (v1): 30 days prior to admission [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2]  
- New plan (v2): 60 days prior to admission [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How did the cataract waiting period change between the old and new Apex plan?
records.answer: The cataract waiting period was shortened from **24 months in the old Apex Health Shield Policy (Version 1)** to **12 months in the new Apex Health Shield Policy (Version 2)**, effectively cutting the waiting period in half. [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: Which version of the Apex plan has the shorter wait for conditions declared at purchase?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield Version 2 (2024 Revised) has the shorter waiting period for conditions declared at purchase. It requires a 36‑month waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception, compared with 48 months in Version 1 [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: How did the co-payment for senior citizens change between the two Apex versions?
records.answer:
The mandatory co‑payment for insured persons aged 65 years and older was cut in half.  
In Version 1 it was 20 % of each admissible claim [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.6], whereas in Version 2 it was reduced to 10 % per claim [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: Does the critical illness rider cover stem cell transplants for sickle cell disease?
records.answer:
The Critical Illness Rider lists **Major Organ / Bone Marrow Transplant** as a covered illness, providing a lump‑sum benefit of 100 % of the Rider Sum Insured with a 30‑day survival period[SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].  
However, the policy documents do not mention sickle cell disease or specify that stem‑cell transplants for that condition are covered. Therefore, while bone‑marrow (stem‑cell) transplants are covered under the rider, the policy does not provide evidence that it covers transplants specifically for sickle cell disease.
